import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Find features with strong effect sizes (|mean_y1-mean_y0| > 0.4)
    effects = [(feats.ids[i], abs(feats.y.mean() - feats.y[feats.x[:,i] > feats.x[:,i].mean()].mean())) 
               for i in range(len(feats.ids))]
    strong_features = [fid for fid, effect in effects if effect > 0.4]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated pairs with |r| >= 0.6)
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                fid1, fid2 = feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]
                correlated_pairs.add((min(fid1,fid2), max(fid1,fid2)))
    
    # Build a set of unique features (remove duplicates)
    unique_features = set(strong_features)
    for pair in correlated_pairs:
        if pair[0] in unique_features and pair[1] in unique_features:
            unique_features.remove(pair[1])  # Keep first, remove second
    
    # Look for product terms among remaining features
    candidates = list(unique_features)
    best_product = None
    best_p = 1.0
    best_effect = 0.0
    
    # Try all pairs of features to find significant product terms
    for i in range(len(candidates)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(candidates)):
            fid1, fid2 = candidates[i], candidates[j]
            # Create product feature
            prod = feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)] * feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)]
            
            # Test significance using t-test
            y1 = prod[feats.y == 1]
            y0 = prod[feats.y == 0]
            if len(y1) > 0 and len(y0) > 0:
                t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
                effect_size = abs(y1.mean() - y0.mean())
                
                if p_val < best_p and effect_size > 0.05:
                    best_p = p_val
                    best_product = (fid1, fid2)
                    best_effect = effect_size
    
    # If we found a good product term, return it
    if best_product and best_p < 0.05:
        return Design(
            drivers=(best_product[0], best_product[1]),
            columns=(best_product[0], best_product[1]),
            products=(best_product,),
            loadings={}
        )
    
    # Otherwise, return top individual features
    top_features = sorted(strong_features, key=lambda f: abs(feats.y.mean() - feats.y[feats.x[:, feats.column(f)] > feats.x[:, feats.column(f)].mean()].mean()), reverse=True)[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    return Design(
        drivers=tuple(top_features),
        columns=tuple(top_features),
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
